Which statement is correct?
A
The wave has a period of 2 s and could be either transverse or longitudinal.
B
The wave has a period of 2 s and must be transverse.
C
The wave has a period of 4 s and could be either transverse or longitudinal.
D
The wave has a period of 4 s and must be transverse.

hints: Look at the time axis in s and find when the particle first returns to the same displacement moving in the same direction as at $0\text{ s}$.
Compare the zero crossings at $0\text{ s}$, $2\text{ s}$ and $4\text{ s}$ - check the slope direction to decide which interval is one full period $T$.
Ask what transverse or longitudinal means - direction of vibration compared with direction of energy transfer - and whether a displacement against time graph shows that direction.
walkthrough: Identify what is plotted: displacement in $\text{cm}$ of one particle against time in $\text{s}$, so the time for the motion to repeat exactly is the period $T$.

Follow the curve from $0\text{ s}$ where displacement is $0$ and increasing, through maximum $+2\text{ cm}$ near $1\text{ s}$, back to $0$ at $2\text{ s}$ but now decreasing, then to $-2\text{ cm}$ near $3\text{ s}$.
Note the motion only returns to $0$ and increasing again at $4\text{ s}$, so $T = 4\text{ s} - 0\text{ s} = 4\text{ s}$; the $2\text{ s}$ interval is a half oscillation.

Recall that transverse means vibration perpendicular to energy travel and longitudinal means vibration parallel to energy travel; a graph of displacement magnitude against time does not show the spatial direction.
Therefore the wave has period $4\text{ s}$ and could be either type. This is option C

A.explanation: The time for a full oscillation is not $2\text{ s}$; $2\text{ s}$ is only the time from zero to zero with opposite slope, which is half a cycle.

B.explanation: The period is not $2\text{ s}$ and a displacement-time graph does not prove the vibration is perpendicular to energy transfer.

C.explanation: The oscillation repeats every $4\text{ s}$ and a displacement-time graph can be produced by either transverse or longitudinal vibration.

D.explanation: The period of $4\text{ s}$ is correct, but the graph does not show direction relative to wave travel so it need not be transverse.
